near_miss.lead: nefna sér vátta / ganga at dómi (legal witness-naming formula)
near_miss.why_not: Only ON partners share the formula (same branch, same text); the Armenian partners have anown kočʻem 'be called by name', unrelated.

The Irish is the natural-produce list of the ruler's-truth or curse type (usce a iasc, caill a mes, talam a thorad); the ON passages are plain landscape description (lake full of fish). Shared roots, but generic and not the same context. The best match for the Irish motif, Od. 19.113 (sea yields fish under a just king), has no cognate words.
Irish 'Fír tra' is an assent ('true indeed'); the Latin is ius iurandum uerum 'a true oath'. Different collocation.

near_miss.lead: fell hann dauðr til jarðar 'fell dead to earth'
near_miss.why_not: The Thucydides partners are unrelated. A possible partner, Hom. ἔραζε (*h₁er-), uses a non-cognate verb and cannot be searched because adverbs are not indexed as content words. Falling dead to the ground is too generic anyway.
No partner has the taunt; the Greek partners are unrelated.

near_miss.lead: kin terms (mother/daughter/sister); self-naming 'nefndisk X ok kvazk vera' ~ OE 'X is mīn nama (cwæð hē), ic eom'
near_miss.why_not: Kin-term lists are generic. Self-identification with kveða/cweþan is Germanic-internal only (ON and OE are the same branch), and it is generic.

near_miss.lead: OIr oath 'tongu do dia toinges mo thúath' (túath ~ ON þjóð)
near_miss.why_not: The ON partners use þjóð in non-oath contexts (king over many peoples; drótt þjóð). No cognate oath formula in the bundles.
Irish 'ubull a brága' (the hound's throat) against Iðunn's apples: no shared context.
Narrative snowfall against a ritual list of weather-woes; generic.
The pair occurs everywhere; the pivot (named after his mother, who outlived his father) has no congruent figure in any partner.

near_miss.lead: 'swift horses' lúatha mairc ~ ON marr + fljótr?
near_miss.why_not: I checked: ON 'fyllar mars' is a ship kenning, and 'fljóts annan veg' means 'on the other side of the Fljót' (Lagarfljót, the saga's river), not the adjective fljótr. No epithet + noun match.

near_miss.lead: ON hǫggva ... lemja (arm broken) ~ Russ. skovany ... perelomany (limbs fettered, broken)
near_miss.why_not: Two cognate verb pairs, but hǫggva 'hew' and kovat' 'forge, fetter' differ in sense, the scenes are not congruent, the byliny are late, and 'break a limb' is generic.
ON is a sword taboo (the sun must not shine on the hilts); Serbian marks time of day (before sunrise). Generic subject + verb with no shared context; Vuk is late.

near_miss.lead: beasts of battle: 'hrafn létum ná svelgja'
near_miss.why_not: None of the Irish partners has the motif; outside Germanic the motif is carried by non-cognate words (Il. 1.4-5), so I made no search lead.
ON is a calendar computation and AV a list of seasons; shared season vocabulary only.
The partners are unrelated. Homeric μαλακοῖσι/μειλιχίοισι ἐπέεσσι is a renewal with no cognate word, too weak for a lead.

near_miss.lead: Þórr ~ toirnech and tǫnn ~ dét co-occurring
near_miss.why_not: Coincidence: a walrus-ivory image of Thor in a pouch, against the thunder of battle and ivory-hilted swords (calg ṅdét). No shared collocation.

near_miss.lead: (various: karl inn skegglausi; vébǫnd court ring; feast; death of Lóegaire; fír do gaile; fear in the breast; víg vegit)
near_miss.why_not: On close reading none of the partners shares wording or a congruent context.

error.correct_reading: Gunnarr (personal name), unmapped; if it is etymologized at all, gunnr < *gʷʰn̥-
error.evidence: The personal name Gunnarr is mapped to *kóryos 'army'. The same error recurs in BS-a447e (AM-132-fol-Njals-saga 12r:29).

error.correct_reading: Hróðný, a woman's name ('móðir hans hét Hróðný'), should be unmapped
nár 'corpse', acc. pl. ná (*neḱ-): 'hrafn létum ná svelgja' = 'we let the raven swallow corpses'
fóirithin, verbal noun of fo-reith 'helps, succours' (fo- < *upo + reithid < *Hret-)
error.evidence: Mapped to *upér via a lemma fóir.

note: Second reader of 33 flagged bundles. No claims: every lead was generic, Germanic-internal, or the contexts were not congruent. 18 near-miss lines (one groups 7 empty bundles), 5 error reports.
